subject: Culture
title: Honor in the American South
description: One-minute skill: Honor in the American South.

hook.text: Psychologists insulted students in a hallway. Southerners' cortisol spiked. Northerners shrugged.

buildup.text: Richard Nisbett traced southern honor culture to Scots-Irish herders who settled the backcountry.

discovery.text: Herders had no fences or police. Projecting toughness was the only way to protect livestock.

twist.text: Centuries later, those counties still have higher argument-based homicide rates than farming regions.

climax.text: Culture of honor explains why 'stand your ground' laws passed easily in former herding states.

punchline.text: Herding vanished. The reflexes it built did not.

quiz.question: Who linked southern US honor culture to herding ancestry?
